small_guidance:
- The fused tail is already cheap; the conv dominates. Minor tail tuning (TILE_W=32, num_warps=2) won't close the gap. Focus tuning effort on a custom conv kernel instead.
- If keeping the current tail, sweep TILE_W ∈ {16, 32, 64} with num_warps ∈ {2, 4} and num_stages=2 — but expect <5% impact on end-to-end runtime.
- Ensure the conv output is in `channels_last_3d` if a custom conv is added, so the LSE reduction across C becomes contiguous.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), with implicit im2col gather (compute D/H/W input offsets inline). Shapes here (N=4, OC=64, D=32, H=128, W=128, K=3) give a GEMM of M=OC=64, N=spatial=524288, K=IC*27=864 — pick BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64–128, BLOCK_K=32, autotune num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3}.
- Fuse the 2×2×2 maxpool, channel-wise logsumexp, and ReLU directly into the conv epilogue: have the conv kernel write OC×(2³ pool-window) values to registers/shared memory, max-reduce across the window, then LSE-reduce across OC, then ReLU — eliminating the intermediate `[N, 64, 32, 128, 128]` tensor (the dominant memory traffic). This requires the conv kernel to tile output spatially in multiples of 2 and own the full OC dim per program, so use BLOCK_OC=64 (full), BLOCK_N=8 pooled outputs (=16 raw spatial).
- If full fusion is too complex, at minimum write the conv as a custom kernel and keep the existing pool+LSE+ReLU tail — the conv alone is the >90% cost.
